items.q: Two heterozygous parents, both Aa, produce 200 offspring. Give the number expected to show the recessive character.
items.s: The recessive class is one part of four; 200 / 4 = 50.

items.q: A heterozygote Aa is mated with a homozygous recessive aa and 308 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to show the recessive character.
items.s: Half the reproductive cells of the heterozygote carry the hidden form; 308 / 2 = 154.

items.q: An individual is heterozygous at 8 independently assorting loci and homozygous at the rest. State the number of kinds of reproductive cell it can form.
items.s: Each heterozygous locus doubles the number of kinds; 2 ^ 8 = 256.

items.q: Two heterozygotes are crossed and 748 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be homozygous dominant.
items.s: One quarter of the progeny are pure for the dominant form; 748 / 4 = 187.

items.q: Aa is crossed with Aa and 956 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be heterozygous.
items.s: Half the progeny of two heterozygotes carry two different forms; 956 / 2 = 478.

items.q: One form of a gene is not completely dominant over the other, so three classes appear in the ratio one to two to one. Of 800 offspring, give the number in the middle class.
items.s: The middle class fills two parts of four; 2 x 800 / 4 = 400.

items.q: A messenger molecule carries 825 bases in its coding region. State the number of triplets it contains.
items.s: Each triplet is three bases long; 825 / 3 = 275.

items.q: Two carriers of a recessive condition have 4 children. State the probability that none of them shows the condition, to four decimal places.
items.s: Each child escapes with probability three quarters, and the children are independent; 0.75 ^ 4 = 0.3164.

items.q: A gene is 5600 bases long on the strand that is copied and the copying enzyme adds 30 bases each second. State the time taken to copy it, in seconds.
items.s: The time is the length divided by the rate; 5600 / 30 = 186.

items.q: A parent is heterozygous at 4 loci lying on different structures. State the probability that a reproductive cell carries the maternal form at every one of them, to four decimal places.
items.s: Every locus is decided independently with probability one half; 0.5 ^ 4 = 0.0625.

items.q: A species has a haploid count of 8. State the diploid count of its body cells.
items.s: A body cell carries both members of every pair; 2 x 8 = 16.

items.q: A sample of 482 diploid individuals is taken from a population. State the number of copies of an autosomal gene present in the sample.
items.s: Every diploid individual carries two copies; 2 x 482 = 964.

items.q: Two parents heterozygous at both of two independently assorting loci are crossed and 864 offspring are obtained. Give the number expected to show both dominant characters.
items.s: The double dominant class fills nine parts of sixteen; 9 x 864 / 16 = 486.

items.q: In a cross between two double heterozygotes, 2016 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to show the dominant character of the first locus with the hidden character of the second.
items.s: That class fills three parts of sixteen; 3 x 2016 / 16 = 378.

items.q: A cross between two individuals heterozygous at both of two loci gives 2496 offspring. Give the number expected to show both hidden characters.
items.s: The double hidden class fills one part of sixteen; 2496 / 16 = 156.

items.q: A test cross yields 14 recombinant offspring out of 400 examined. State the distance between the two loci in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The separation in map units is the percentage of recombinants; 100 x 14 / 400 = 3.5.

items.q: Two loci lie 34 map units apart and 400 offspring are produced by a test cross. Give the number of recombinant offspring expected.
items.s: The recombining fraction is 34 per cent of the progeny; 34 x 400 / 100 = 136.

items.q: In a sample of double stranded deoxyribonucleic acid, adenine makes up 29 per cent of the bases. State the percentage of guanine.
items.s: Thymine also takes 29 per cent, leaving 42 per cent shared equally by the other two bases; 42 / 2 = 21.

items.q: Two classes appear in the ratio 12 to 4 and 1952 offspring are counted. Give the number expected in the first class.
items.s: The parts of the ratio total 16, so the first class holds 12 of them; 12 x 1952 / 16 = 1464.

items.q: In a dihybrid cross giving four classes in the ratio nine to three to three to one, 1136 offspring are counted. Give the number showing the dominant character of the first locus whatever the second locus shows.
items.s: The classes showing that dominant character hold nine and three parts, twelve in all; 12 x 1136 / 16 = 852.

items.q: A recessive lethal form leaves a living ratio of two to one and 324 living offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be heterozygous.
items.s: Two thirds of the living progeny carry two different forms; 2 x 324 / 3 = 216.

items.q: Two genes interact so that the offspring fall into two classes in the ratio nine to seven, and 1728 offspring are counted. Give the number in the smaller class.
items.s: The smaller class fills seven parts of sixteen; 7 x 1728 / 16 = 756.

items.q: A carrier mother is mated with a normal father and 244 sons are born. Give the number of sons expected to show the recessive sex linked character.
items.s: Half the sons receive the changed structure from the mother; 244 / 2 = 122.

items.q: Chiasmata are seen in 68 per cent of the cells examined between two loci. State the distance between the loci in map units.
items.s: Each exchange involves two of the four threads, so half the cells give recombinants; 68 / 2 = 34.

items.q: Locus B lies 14 map units from A and locus C lies 15 map units from B on the same side. State the distance from A to C.
items.s: Distances along one structure add; 14 + 15 = 29.

items.q: Two intervals are 26 and 18 map units long and 8000 offspring are examined. Give the number of double crossovers expected if exchanges occur independently.
items.s: The expected fraction is the product of the two frequencies; 26 x 18 x 8000 / 10000 = 374.

items.q: The number of double crossovers expected in a sample is 40 and 6 are actually seen. State the coefficient of interference, to two decimal places.
items.s: The coincidence is 6 divided by 40, so the interference is one minus that; 1 - 6 / 40 = 0.85.

items.q: The number of double crossovers expected in a sample is 18 and 8 are observed. State the coefficient of coincidence to four decimal places.
items.s: The coefficient is the observed count divided by the expected count; 8 / 18 = 0.4444.

items.q: In a population of 50000 diploid individuals, 2 new changes are found at one locus. State the rate of change per gene copy.
items.s: There are two copies in each individual, so 2 x 50000 = 100000 copies carry the changes; 2 / 100000 = 0.00002.

items.q: A locus has 7 forms in a population and diploid individuals are examined. State the number of different genotypes possible at that locus.
items.s: The count includes the pairs of like forms and the pairs of unlike forms; 7 x 8 / 2 = 28.

items.q: A gene is 1551 base pairs long and 93 of those base pairs lie in introns. State the number of amino acids in the protein made from it.
items.s: The coding length is 1551 minus 93, and each amino acid takes three bases; (1551 - 93) / 3 = 486.

items.q: A protein contains 129 amino acid units and each unit has an average mass of 110 units. State the mass of the protein in the same units.
items.s: The total is the count multiplied by the average mass; 110 x 129 = 14190.

items.q: A class expected to form 75 per cent of 468 offspring actually appears 344 times. State the percentage deviation from the expectation, to two decimal places.
items.s: The expectation is 75 per cent of 468, which is 351, so the deviation is -7 against 351; 100 x -7 / 351 = -1.99.

items.q: Two carriers of a recessive condition have 5 children. State the probability that exactly two of them show the condition, to four decimal places.
items.s: Each child is affected with probability one quarter, and the two affected may fall in any of 10 positions; 6 x 0.0625 x 0.4219 = 0.2637.

items.q: In a three point cross the first interval shows 750 single crossovers, the second 700, and 105 double crossovers, with 378 of each parental kind. State the corrected distance of the first interval in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The sample holds 2416 offspring, and the first interval counts its singles plus the doubles; 100 x 855 / 2416 = 35.39.

items.q: Two intervals of 11 and 17 map units are added directly, so the double crossover class has been counted twice. State the distance between the outer loci after removing the double counting, to two decimal places.
items.s: The direct total is 11 + 17, and the doubles enter twice so once must be taken away; 11 + 17 - 2 x 11 x 17 / 100 = 24.26.

items.q: Intervals of 10 and 9 map units lie in a sample of 3000 offspring, and the coefficient of coincidence is 0.6. State the number of double crossovers observed.
items.s: The expected count is 10 x 9 x 3000 / 10000 = 27, and the coincidence scales it; 27 x 0.6 = 16.

items.q: A protein is 300 amino acids long and the assembling particle adds 15 units each second. State the time taken to build it, in seconds.
items.s: The time is the length divided by the rate; 300 / 15 = 20.

items.q: A test cross gives 173 offspring of each parental kind and 41 plus 39 recombinant kinds. State the distance between the two loci in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The two parental kinds give 346 offspring and the sample totals 426; 100 x 80 / 426 = 18.78.

items.q: A coding region of a messenger molecule is 1512 bases long and its last triplet is a stop signal. State the number of amino acids in the protein made.
items.s: The region holds 504 triplets and the stop signal codes for no amino acid; 504 - 1 = 503.

items.q: Two double heterozygotes are crossed and 1696 offspring are counted. Assuming the two loci interact so that only the double recessive class is affected, give the number expected to be affected.
items.s: The affected class fills one part of sixteen; 1696 / 16 = 106.

items.q: A genome has 2000000 base pairs and the rate of change is one base pair in every hundred million per generation. State the number of new changes appearing in one genome in a million generations.
items.s: Each generation brings 2000000 divided by a hundred million changes, and a million generations multiply that by a million; 2000000 x 0.00000001 x 1000000 = 20000.

items.q: Two unaffected sibs of an affected child each have a two thirds chance of being carriers. State the probability that their first child is affected, to four decimal places.
items.s: Both must be carriers before the child can be affected; 0.6667 x 0.6667 x 0.25 = 0.1111.

items.q: Intervals of 24 and 30 map units separate three loci in that order. State the expected proportion of double crossovers if exchanges are independent, to four decimal places.
items.s: Each interval recombines with its own frequency, and the two must happen together; 24 x 30 / 10000 = 0.072.

items.q: Two loci lie 2 map units apart and 1800 offspring are scored. State the number of offspring that are expected to be parental for both loci.
items.s: The recombinant share is 2 per cent, so the parental share is the rest; 1800 - 2 x 1800 / 100 = 36.

autosome
hemizygous
Barr body

items.q: Which of the following best describes transcription?

a change in which a segment of a structure is turned round and rejoined
a stock that gives offspring like itself in every generation for the character followed
a unit of inheritance that alters the degree to which another one shows its effect

items.q: Which of the following best describes Punnett square?

one of the two identical threads formed when a structure duplicates before division
a change that alters the grouping of bases by adding or losing bases not in threes
a grid listing all the possible unions of male and female reproductive cells

items.q: Which statement correctly defines reading frame?

the offspring obtained by mating members of the first filial group among themselves
a change that alters the grouping of bases by adding or losing bases not in threes
the grouping of bases into triplets that fixes how a message is interpreted

items.q: Which term is described by “the observed count of double exchanges divided by the count expected from the two distances”?

map unit
coupling phase
coefficient of coincidence

items.q: Which statement correctly defines dominant allele?

the proportion of individuals carrying a form of a gene who actually show the expected character
the form of a gene that shows its effect even when a different form is present
the reduction in the chance of a second exchange close to a first one

items.q: The statement “the category that produces only one kind of reproductive cell with respect to the structures deciding maleness” describes which of the following?

a swap of segments between the two identical threads of one duplicated structure
a part of a gene that is removed from the message before it is used
a grid listing all the possible unions of male and female reproductive cells

homozygous
monohybrid cross
genotype

codominance

codominance

phenotype

items.q: Which term is described by “a change in a body cell, which is not passed to the offspring”?

somatic mutation

the region at which the copying enzyme binds to begin making a message
a structure carrying genes that plays no part in deciding the sex of an organism
a mating of an individual of unknown constitution with one that shows the hidden form

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines coupling phase.

a change in a body cell, which is not passed to the offspring
the arrangement in which the two dominant forms lie on the same member of a pair
the production of new combinations of gene forms by exchange between structures

items.q: Which statement correctly defines haploid number?

the observed count of double exchanges divided by the count expected from the two distances
a structure carrying the genes which decide whether an organism develops as male or female
the random distribution of members of different gene pairs among reproductive cells so that one pair does not influence another
items.s: haploid number: the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair. The other options describe coefficient of coincidence, independent assortment, sex chromosome.

items.q: The statement “the separation of the two forms of a gene into different reproductive cells during meiosis” describes which of the following?

independent assortment
segregation
test cross

items.q: Which of the following best describes dominant allele?

the situation in which the two forms blend so that the hybrid lies between the two pure lines
a form of a gene that causes death when carried in two copies
the form of a gene that shows its effect even when a different form is present

items.q: The statement “the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair” describes which of the following?

diploid number
haploid number
centromere

mutagen
polyploidy

the observed count of double exchanges divided by the count expected from the two distances
the tendency of genes lying on the same structure to be inherited together
a mating followed through one pair of contrasting characters only

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines diploid number.
o: the arrangement in which a dominant form and a hidden form lie on the same member of a pair
the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme
carrying two different forms of a gene at the same place on the two partner structures
the total count of structures in a cell that carries both members of each pair
items.s: diploid number: the total count of structures in a cell that carries both members of each pair. The other options describe repulsion phase, parental generation, heterozygous.

o: synapsis
sister chromatid exchange
homologous chromosomes
centromere

induced mutation
spontaneous mutation
inversion

codon
translation
transcription

a line drawing in which the order of genes and the distances between them are shown
a change of one base pair in the sequence of a gene
a trait whose expression differs between the two sexes because of the hormonal background

the control of several unrelated characters by a single gene

point mutation
mutagen

items.q: parental generation may be defined as
o: carrying two different forms of a gene at the same place on the two partner structures
a pair of matings in which the characters contributed by the two parents are interchanged
the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme
the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair
items.s: parental generation: the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme. The other options describe haploid number, reciprocal cross, heterozygous.

items.q: translation may be defined as
o: a trait expressed in only one of the two sexes although the genes for it lie in both
the building of a chain of amino acids using the message carried by ribonucleic acid
the grouping of bases into triplets that fixes how a message is interpreted
the category that produces two kinds of reproductive cell with respect to the structures deciding maleness
items.s: translation: the building of a chain of amino acids using the message carried by ribonucleic acid. The other options describe reading frame, heterogametic sex, sex limited character.

items.q: All of the following belong to Linkage and crossing over EXCEPT
o: linkage
codominance
chiasma
crossing over
items.s: Every other option belongs to Linkage and crossing over. “codominance” belongs to Deviations from Mendelian ratios, not Linkage and crossing over.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines interference.
o: the situation in which both forms of a gene are fully expressed in the same individual
the reduction in the chance of a second exchange close to a first one
the paired structures that carry the same set of genes and lie together during meiosis
the offspring obtained by mating members of the first filial group among themselves
items.s: interference: the reduction in the chance of a second exchange close to a first one. The other options describe codominance, homologous chromosomes, F2 generation.

items.q: Which term is described by “a triplet of bases that specifies one amino acid”?
o: intron
promoter
transcription
codon
items.s: codon is a triplet of bases that specifies one amino acid.

items.q: Which term is described by “a structure carrying the genes which decide whether an organism develops as male or female”?
o: homogametic sex
sex limited character
sex influenced character
sex chromosome
items.s: sex chromosome is a structure carrying the genes which decide whether an organism develops as male or female.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines exon?
o: the form of a gene that shows its effect even when a different form is present
the pairing of corresponding structures along their length before any exchange takes place
a part of a gene that is retained in the mature message
the proportion of individuals carrying a form of a gene who actually show the expected character
items.s: exon: a part of a gene that is retained in the mature message. The other options describe dominant allele, synapsis, penetrance.

items.q: Which term is described by “the triplet of bases on a transfer molecule that pairs with a triplet of the message”?
o: promoter
reading frame
ribosome
anticodon
items.s: anticodon is the triplet of bases on a transfer molecule that pairs with a triplet of the message.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines gamete?
o: the paired structures that carry the same set of genes and lie together during meiosis
the arrangement in which a dominant form and a hidden form lie on the same member of a pair
a reproductive cell that carries a single set of structures bearing the genes
the separation of the two forms of a gene into different reproductive cells during meiosis
items.s: gamete: a reproductive cell that carries a single set of structures bearing the genes. The other options describe segregation, repulsion phase, homologous chromosomes.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines interference?
o: the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme
the arrangement in which the two dominant forms lie on the same member of a pair
a change in a body cell, which is not passed to the offspring
the reduction in the chance of a second exchange close to a first one
items.s: interference: the reduction in the chance of a second exchange close to a first one. The other options describe parental generation, somatic mutation, coupling phase.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines spontaneous mutation?
o: one of the two identical threads formed when a structure duplicates before division
the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme
a change that arises without any outside agent being applied
a stock that gives offspring like itself in every generation for the character followed
items.s: spontaneous mutation: a change that arises without any outside agent being applied. The other options describe chromatid, parental generation, true breeding line.

items.q: The statement “a change that alters the grouping of bases by adding or losing bases not in threes” describes which of the following?
o: induced mutation
somatic mutation
inversion
frameshift
items.s: frameshift is a change that alters the grouping of bases by adding or losing bases not in threes.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines polyploidy.
o: a grid listing all the possible unions of male and female reproductive cells
a structure carrying genes that plays no part in deciding the sex of an organism
the building of a chain of amino acids using the message carried by ribonucleic acid
the condition of having more than two complete sets of structures bearing the genes in a cell
items.s: polyploidy: the condition of having more than two complete sets of structures bearing the genes in a cell. The other options describe translation, autosome, Punnett square.

items.q: The statement “carrying only one copy of a gene because the partner structure lacks that region” describes which of the following?
o: hemizygous
sex chromosome
sex limited character
autosome
items.s: hemizygous is carrying only one copy of a gene because the partner structure lacks that region.

items.q: karyotype may be defined as
o: the ordered display of the structures of a cell according to size and shape
the reduction in the chance of a second exchange close to a first one
a change in a body cell, which is not passed to the offspring
a structure carrying genes that plays no part in deciding the sex of an organism
items.s: karyotype: the ordered display of the structures of a cell according to size and shape. The other options describe autosome, somatic mutation, interference.

items.q: Which of the following best describes haploid number?
o: the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair
the hiding of the effect of one gene by a different gene at another place
the pairing of corresponding structures along their length before any exchange takes place
a part of a gene that is retained in the mature message
items.s: haploid number: the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair. The other options describe synapsis, exon, epistasis.

items.q: Which term is described by “the passing of a character from a father to his daughters and then to his grandsons”?
o: homogametic sex
heterogametic sex
Barr body
criss cross inheritance
items.s: criss cross inheritance is the passing of a character from a father to his daughters and then to his grandsons.

items.q: Which term is described by “the production of new combinations of gene forms by exchange between structures”?
o: homologous chromosomes
chromatid
recombination
haploid number
items.s: recombination is the production of new combinations of gene forms by exchange between structures.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines synapsis.
o: the pairing of corresponding structures along their length before any exchange takes place
carrying two identical forms of a gene at the same place on the two partner structures
a structure carrying genes that plays no part in deciding the sex of an organism
one of the two identical threads formed when a structure duplicates before division
items.s: synapsis: the pairing of corresponding structures along their length before any exchange takes place. The other options describe homozygous, autosome, chromatid.

items.q: In a cross between two double heterozygotes, 1520 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to show the dominant character of the first locus with the hidden character of the second.
items.s: That class fills three parts of sixteen; 3 x 1520 / 16 = 285.

items.q: A test cross yields 68 recombinant offspring out of 400 examined. State the distance between the two loci in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The separation in map units is the percentage of recombinants; 100 x 68 / 400 = 17.

items.q: Two loci lie 30 map units apart and 600 offspring are produced by a test cross. Give the number of recombinant offspring expected.
items.s: The recombining fraction is 30 per cent of the progeny; 30 x 600 / 100 = 180.

items.q: In a sample of double stranded deoxyribonucleic acid, adenine makes up 18 per cent of the bases. State the percentage of guanine.
items.s: Thymine also takes 18 per cent, leaving 64 per cent shared equally by the other two bases; 64 / 2 = 32.

items.q: A carrier mother is mated with a normal father and 122 sons are born. Give the number of sons expected to show the recessive sex linked character.
items.s: Half the sons receive the changed structure from the mother; 122 / 2 = 61.

items.q: Locus B lies 15 map units from A and locus C lies 29 map units from B on the same side. State the distance from A to C.
items.s: Distances along one structure add; 15 + 29 = 44.

items.q: The number of double crossovers expected in a sample is 37 and 22 are observed. State the coefficient of coincidence to four decimal places.
items.s: The coefficient is the observed count divided by the expected count; 22 / 37 = 0.5946.

items.q: A protein contains 268 amino acid units and each unit has an average mass of 110 units. State the mass of the protein in the same units.
items.s: The total is the count multiplied by the average mass; 110 x 268 = 29480.

items.q: A protein is 320 amino acids long and the assembling particle adds 5 units each second. State the time taken to build it, in seconds.
items.s: The time is the length divided by the rate; 320 / 5 = 64.

items.q: Two loci lie 5 map units apart and 1400 offspring are scored. State the number of offspring that are expected to be parental for both loci.
items.s: The recombinant share is 5 per cent, so the parental share is the rest; 1400 - 5 x 1400 / 100 = 70.

items.q: Two heterozygous parents, both Aa, produce 632 offspring. Give the number expected to show the dominant character.
items.s: A cross of two heterozygotes gives three dominant to one recessive, so the dominant class holds three parts of four; 3 x 632 / 4 = 474.

items.q: Two heterozygous parents, both Aa, produce 816 offspring. Give the number expected to show the recessive character.
items.s: The recessive class is one part of four; 816 / 4 = 204.

items.q: A heterozygote Aa is mated with a homozygous recessive aa and 200 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to show the recessive character.
items.s: Half the reproductive cells of the heterozygote carry the hidden form; 200 / 2 = 100.

items.q: An individual is heterozygous at 6 independently assorting loci and homozygous at the rest. State the number of kinds of reproductive cell it can form.
items.s: Each heterozygous locus doubles the number of kinds; 2 ^ 6 = 64.

items.q: Two heterozygotes are crossed and 712 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be homozygous dominant.
items.s: One quarter of the progeny are pure for the dominant form; 712 / 4 = 178.

items.q: A sample of 443 diploid individuals is taken from a population. State the number of copies of an autosomal gene present in the sample.
items.s: Every diploid individual carries two copies; 2 x 443 = 886.

items.q: A cross between two individuals heterozygous at both of two loci gives 3104 offspring. Give the number expected to show both hidden characters.
items.s: The double hidden class fills one part of sixteen; 3104 / 16 = 194.

items.q: Aa is crossed with Aa and 672 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be heterozygous.
items.s: Half the progeny of two heterozygotes carry two different forms; 672 / 2 = 336.

items.q: One form of a gene is not completely dominant over the other, so three classes appear in the ratio one to two to one. Of 360 offspring, give the number in the middle class.
items.s: The middle class fills two parts of four; 2 x 360 / 4 = 180.

items.q: Two classes appear in the ratio 9 to 3 and 1080 offspring are counted. Give the number expected in the first class.
items.s: The parts of the ratio total 12, so the first class holds 9 of them; 9 x 1080 / 12 = 810.

items.q: In a dihybrid cross giving four classes in the ratio nine to three to three to one, 960 offspring are counted. Give the number showing the dominant character of the first locus whatever the second locus shows.
items.s: The classes showing that dominant character hold nine and three parts, twelve in all; 12 x 960 / 16 = 720.

items.q: A recessive lethal form leaves a living ratio of two to one and 255 living offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be heterozygous.
items.s: Two thirds of the living progeny carry two different forms; 2 x 255 / 3 = 170.

items.q: Two genes interact so that the offspring fall into two classes in the ratio nine to seven, and 1088 offspring are counted. Give the number in the smaller class.
items.s: The smaller class fills seven parts of sixteen; 7 x 1088 / 16 = 476.

items.q: Chiasmata are seen in 90 per cent of the cells examined between two loci. State the distance between the loci in map units.
items.s: Each exchange involves two of the four threads, so half the cells give recombinants; 90 / 2 = 45.

items.q: Two intervals are 17 and 26 map units long and 3000 offspring are examined. Give the number of double crossovers expected if exchanges occur independently.
items.s: The expected fraction is the product of the two frequencies; 17 x 26 x 3000 / 10000 = 132.

items.q: The number of double crossovers expected in a sample is 40 and 16 are actually seen. State the coefficient of interference, to two decimal places.
items.s: The coincidence is 16 divided by 40, so the interference is one minus that; 1 - 16 / 40 = 0.6.

items.q: In a population of 200000 diploid individuals, 13 new changes are found at one locus. State the rate of change per gene copy.
items.s: There are two copies in each individual, so 2 x 200000 = 400000 copies carry the changes; 13 / 400000 = 0.000032.

items.q: A gene is 888 base pairs long and 180 of those base pairs lie in introns. State the number of amino acids in the protein made from it.
items.s: The coding length is 888 minus 180, and each amino acid takes three bases; (888 - 180) / 3 = 236.

items.q: A class expected to form 25 per cent of 584 offspring actually appears 141 times. State the percentage deviation from the expectation, to two decimal places.
items.s: The expectation is 25 per cent of 584, which is 146, so the deviation is -5 against 146; 100 x -5 / 146 = -3.42.

items.q: A messenger molecule carries 438 bases in its coding region. State the number of triplets it contains.
items.s: Each triplet is three bases long; 438 / 3 = 146.

items.q: Two carriers of a recessive condition have 3 children. State the probability that none of them shows the condition, to four decimal places.
items.s: Each child escapes with probability three quarters, and the children are independent; 0.75 ^ 3 = 0.4219.

items.q: In a three point cross the first interval shows 1400 single crossovers, the second 950, and 266 double crossovers, with 311 of each parental kind. State the corrected distance of the first interval in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The sample holds 3504 offspring, and the first interval counts its singles plus the doubles; 100 x 1666 / 3504 = 47.55.

items.q: Two intervals of 8 and 7 map units are added directly, so the double crossover class has been counted twice. State the distance between the outer loci after removing the double counting, to two decimal places.
items.s: The direct total is 8 + 7, and the doubles enter twice so once must be taken away; 8 + 7 - 2 x 8 x 7 / 100 = 13.88.

items.q: Intervals of 18 and 25 map units lie in a sample of 3000 offspring, and the coefficient of coincidence is 0.6. State the number of double crossovers observed.
items.s: The expected count is 18 x 25 x 3000 / 10000 = 135, and the coincidence scales it; 135 x 0.6 = 81.

items.q: A gene is 2000 bases long on the strand that is copied and the copying enzyme adds 30 bases each second. State the time taken to copy it, in seconds.
items.s: The time is the length divided by the rate; 2000 / 30 = 66.

items.q: A test cross gives 149 offspring of each parental kind and 32 plus 18 recombinant kinds. State the distance between the two loci in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The two parental kinds give 298 offspring and the sample totals 348; 100 x 50 / 348 = 14.37.

items.q: A coding region of a messenger molecule is 2040 bases long and its last triplet is a stop signal. State the number of amino acids in the protein made.
items.s: The region holds 680 triplets and the stop signal codes for no amino acid; 680 - 1 = 679.

items.q: A parent is heterozygous at 5 loci lying on different structures. State the probability that a reproductive cell carries the maternal form at every one of them, to four decimal places.
items.s: Every locus is decided independently with probability one half; 0.5 ^ 5 = 0.0312.

items.q: Two double heterozygotes are crossed and 672 offspring are counted. Assuming the two loci interact so that only the double recessive class is affected, give the number expected to be affected.
items.s: The affected class fills one part of sixteen; 672 / 16 = 42.

items.q: Intervals of 21 and 12 map units separate three loci in that order. State the expected proportion of double crossovers if exchanges are independent, to four decimal places.
items.s: Each interval recombines with its own frequency, and the two must happen together; 21 x 12 / 10000 = 0.0252.

items.q: Two parents heterozygous at both of two independently assorting loci are crossed and 912 offspring are obtained. Give the number expected to show both dominant characters.
items.s: The double dominant class fills nine parts of sixteen; 9 x 912 / 16 = 513.

items.q: In a cross between two double heterozygotes, 832 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to show the dominant character of the first locus with the hidden character of the second.

items.q: A test cross yields 78 recombinant offspring out of 1000 examined. State the distance between the two loci in map units, to two decimal places.

items.q: Two loci lie 35 map units apart and 300 offspring are produced by a test cross. Give the number of recombinant offspring expected.

items.q: Locus B lies 29 map units from A and locus C lies 26 map units from B on the same side. State the distance from A to C.

items.q: The number of double crossovers expected in a sample is 39 and 34 are observed. State the coefficient of coincidence to four decimal places.

items.q: A protein contains 256 amino acid units and each unit has an average mass of 110 units. State the mass of the protein in the same units.

items.q: Two carriers of a recessive condition have 4 children. State the probability that exactly two of them show the condition, to four decimal places.
items.s: Each child is affected with probability one quarter, and the two affected may fall in any of 6 positions; 6 x 0.0625 x 0.5625 = 0.2109.

items.q: A protein is 580 amino acids long and the assembling particle adds 15 units each second. State the time taken to build it, in seconds.
items.s: The time is the length divided by the rate; 580 / 15 = 38.

items.q: Two loci lie 25 map units apart and 2000 offspring are scored. State the number of offspring that are expected to be parental for both loci.

items.q: Two heterozygous parents, both Aa, produce 416 offspring. Give the number expected to show the dominant character.
items.s: A cross of two heterozygotes gives three dominant to one recessive, so the dominant class holds three parts of four; 3 x 416 / 4 = 312.

items.q: One form of a gene is not completely dominant over the other, so three classes appear in the ratio one to two to one. Of 760 offspring, give the number in the middle class.

items.q: dominant allele is best described as
o: carrying two different forms of a gene at the same place on the two partner structures
a stock that gives offspring like itself in every generation for the character followed
the observable character that an organism actually shows
the form of a gene that shows its effect even when a different form is present

items.q: In this course, pleiotropy refers to

the hiding of the effect of one gene by a different gene at another place
the situation in which the two forms blend so that the hybrid lies between the two pure lines
the control of several unrelated characters by a single gene

the total count of structures in a cell that carries both members of each pair
the ordered display of the structures of a cell according to size and shape
the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair

items.q: The statement “a change that arises without any outside agent being applied” describes which of the following?
o: frameshift
spontaneous mutation
somatic mutation
polyploidy

items.q: The statement “the observed count of double exchanges divided by the count expected from the two distances” describes which of the following?
o: coefficient of coincidence
interference
linkage
genetic map

items.q: In this course, promoter refers to

a part of a gene that is removed from the message before it is used
the grouping of bases into triplets that fixes how a message is interpreted
the region at which the copying enzyme binds to begin making a message

items.q: centromere is best described as
o: the total count of structures in a cell that carries both members of each pair
the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair
the constricted region where the two threads of a duplicated structure are joined
one of the two identical threads formed when a structure duplicates before division

items.q: The best definition of true breeding line among these is

a pair of matings in which the characters contributed by the two parents are interchanged
the pair of gene forms carried by an organism at a stated place
the observable character that an organism actually shows

items.q: Which term is described by “the particle on which amino acids are joined into a chain”?
o: exon
codon
ribosome
intron

hemizygous

the category that produces two kinds of reproductive cell with respect to the structures deciding maleness
a trait whose expression differs between the two sexes because of the hormonal background
a structure carrying genes that plays no part in deciding the sex of an organism

items.q: The statement “the tendency of genes lying on the same structure to be inherited together” describes which of the following?
o: crossing over
interference
linkage
coefficient of coincidence

items.q: Choose the option that explains what frameshift means.

the condition of having more than two complete sets of structures bearing the genes in a cell
a change in which a segment of a structure is turned round and rejoined
a change that arises without any outside agent being applied

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Gene expression basics?
o: sex chromosome
transcription
codon
translation

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the random distribution of members of different gene pairs among reproductive cells so that one pair does not influence another”
o: independent assortment
test cross
parental generation
F2 generation

items.q: In this course, Punnett square refers to

a mating of an offspring with one of its own parents
the separation of the two forms of a gene into different reproductive cells during meiosis
the offspring obtained by mating members of the first filial group among themselves

items.q: Choose the option that explains what reciprocal cross means.

a pair of matings in which the characters contributed by the two parents are interchanged
the observable character that an organism actually shows

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a trait whose expression differs between the two sexes because of the hormonal background”
o: Barr body
sex influenced character
sex chromosome
heterogametic sex

items.q: The statement “the region at which the copying enzyme binds to begin making a message” describes which of the following?
o: translation
reading frame
promoter
anticodon
items.s: promoter is the region at which the copying enzyme binds to begin making a message.

items.q: The best definition of interference among these is

the separation of the two forms of a gene into different reproductive cells during meiosis
a mating of an offspring with one of its own parents
the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme

items.q: In this course, coefficient of coincidence refers to
o: the point at which paired structures are seen to be joined during an exchange
the observed count of double exchanges divided by the count expected from the two distances
the exchange of corresponding segments between paired structures during meiosis
the arrangement in which a dominant form and a hidden form lie on the same member of a pair

items.q: aneuploidy is best described as
o: a change in a body cell, which is not passed to the offspring
the condition of having more than two complete sets of structures bearing the genes in a cell
the condition of having one such structure too many or too few in a cell
a change that arises without any outside agent being applied

o: a part of a gene that is retained in the mature message
the particle on which amino acids are joined into a chain
the copying of a gene into a molecule of ribonucleic acid
a part of a gene that is removed from the message before it is used

items.s: The coincidence is 10 divided by 35, so the interference is one minus that; 1 - 10 / 35 = 0.71.

items.s: The direct total is 10 + 19, and the doubles enter twice so once must be taken away; 10 + 19 - 2 x 10 x 19 / 100 = 25.2.

items.q: Intervals of 21 and 20 map units lie in a sample of 1000 offspring, and the coefficient of coincidence is 0.5. State the number of double crossovers observed.

items.q: A recessive lethal form leaves a living ratio of two to one and 555 living offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be heterozygous.
items.s: Two thirds of the living progeny carry two different forms; 2 x 555 / 3 = 370.

items.q: Two genes interact so that the offspring fall into two classes in the ratio nine to seven, and 1792 offspring are counted. Give the number in the smaller class.
items.s: The smaller class fills seven parts of sixteen; 7 x 1792 / 16 = 784.

items.q: A carrier mother is mated with a normal father and 340 sons are born. Give the number of sons expected to show the recessive sex linked character.
items.s: Half the sons receive the changed structure from the mother; 340 / 2 = 170.

items.q: Locus B lies 17 map units from A and locus C lies 7 map units from B on the same side. State the distance from A to C.
items.s: Distances along one structure add; 17 + 7 = 24.

items.q: The number of double crossovers expected in a sample is 54 and 38 are observed. State the coefficient of coincidence to four decimal places.
items.s: The coefficient is the observed count divided by the expected count; 38 / 54 = 0.7037.

items.q: A locus has 3 forms in a population and diploid individuals are examined. State the number of different genotypes possible at that locus.
items.s: The count includes the pairs of like forms and the pairs of unlike forms; 3 x 4 / 2 = 6.

items.q: A gene is 963 base pairs long and 147 of those base pairs lie in introns. State the number of amino acids in the protein made from it.
items.s: The coding length is 963 minus 147, and each amino acid takes three bases; (963 - 147) / 3 = 272.

items.q: A protein contains 354 amino acid units and each unit has an average mass of 110 units. State the mass of the protein in the same units.
items.s: The total is the count multiplied by the average mass; 110 x 354 = 38940.

items.q: A messenger molecule carries 267 bases in its coding region. State the number of triplets it contains.
items.s: Each triplet is three bases long; 267 / 3 = 89.

items.q: In a three point cross the first interval shows 260 single crossovers, the second 240, and 31 double crossovers, with 301 of each parental kind. State the corrected distance of the first interval in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The sample holds 1164 offspring, and the first interval counts its singles plus the doubles; 100 x 291 / 1164 = 25.

items.q: A gene is 2600 bases long on the strand that is copied and the copying enzyme adds 20 bases each second. State the time taken to copy it, in seconds.
items.s: The time is the length divided by the rate; 2600 / 20 = 130.

items.q: A protein is 190 amino acids long and the assembling particle adds 20 units each second. State the time taken to build it, in seconds.
items.s: The time is the length divided by the rate; 190 / 20 = 9.

items.q: A test cross gives 141 offspring of each parental kind and 16 plus 24 recombinant kinds. State the distance between the two loci in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The two parental kinds give 282 offspring and the sample totals 322; 100 x 40 / 322 = 12.42.

items.q: Two double heterozygotes are crossed and 832 offspring are counted. Assuming the two loci interact so that only the double recessive class is affected, give the number expected to be affected.
items.s: The affected class fills one part of sixteen; 832 / 16 = 52.

items.q: Intervals of 15 and 13 map units separate three loci in that order. State the expected proportion of double crossovers if exchanges are independent, to four decimal places.
items.s: Each interval recombines with its own frequency, and the two must happen together; 15 x 13 / 10000 = 0.0195.

items.q: Two loci lie 2 map units apart and 1200 offspring are scored. State the number of offspring that are expected to be parental for both loci.
items.s: The recombinant share is 2 per cent, so the parental share is the rest; 1200 - 2 x 1200 / 100 = 24.

items.q: In a dihybrid cross giving four classes in the ratio nine to three to three to one, 1104 offspring are counted. Give the number showing the dominant character of the first locus whatever the second locus shows.
items.s: The classes showing that dominant character hold nine and three parts, twelve in all; 12 x 1104 / 16 = 828.

items.q: Chiasmata are seen in 78 per cent of the cells examined between two loci. State the distance between the loci in map units.
items.s: Each exchange involves two of the four threads, so half the cells give recombinants; 78 / 2 = 39.

items.q: Two intervals are 27 and 27 map units long and 7000 offspring are examined. Give the number of double crossovers expected if exchanges occur independently.
items.s: The expected fraction is the product of the two frequencies; 27 x 27 x 7000 / 10000 = 510.

items.q: The number of double crossovers expected in a sample is 17 and 4 are actually seen. State the coefficient of interference, to two decimal places.
items.s: The coincidence is 4 divided by 17, so the interference is one minus that; 1 - 4 / 17 = 0.76.

items.q: In a population of 100000 diploid individuals, 11 new changes are found at one locus. State the rate of change per gene copy.
items.s: There are two copies in each individual, so 2 x 100000 = 200000 copies carry the changes; 11 / 200000 = 0.000055.

items.q: A class expected to form 50 per cent of 292 offspring actually appears 155 times. State the percentage deviation from the expectation, to two decimal places.
items.s: The expectation is 50 per cent of 292, which is 146, so the deviation is 9 against 146; 100 x 9 / 146 = 6.16.

items.q: Two intervals of 14 and 6 map units are added directly, so the double crossover class has been counted twice. State the distance between the outer loci after removing the double counting, to two decimal places.
items.s: The direct total is 14 + 6, and the doubles enter twice so once must be taken away; 14 + 6 - 2 x 14 x 6 / 100 = 18.32.

items.q: Intervals of 21 and 15 map units lie in a sample of 6000 offspring, and the coefficient of coincidence is 0.8. State the number of double crossovers observed.
items.s: The expected count is 21 x 15 x 6000 / 10000 = 189, and the coincidence scales it; 189 x 0.8 = 151.

items.q: A coding region of a messenger molecule is 1257 bases long and its last triplet is a stop signal. State the number of amino acids in the protein made.
items.s: The region holds 419 triplets and the stop signal codes for no amino acid; 419 - 1 = 418.

items.q: Two heterozygous parents, both Aa, produce 476 offspring. Give the number expected to show the dominant character.
items.s: A cross of two heterozygotes gives three dominant to one recessive, so the dominant class holds three parts of four; 3 x 476 / 4 = 357.

items.q: Two heterozygous parents, both Aa, produce 444 offspring. Give the number expected to show the recessive character.
items.s: The recessive class is one part of four; 444 / 4 = 111.

items.q: A heterozygote Aa is mated with a homozygous recessive aa and 300 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to show the recessive character.
items.s: Half the reproductive cells of the heterozygote carry the hidden form; 300 / 2 = 150.

items.q: An individual is heterozygous at 5 independently assorting loci and homozygous at the rest. State the number of kinds of reproductive cell it can form.
items.s: Each heterozygous locus doubles the number of kinds; 2 ^ 5 = 32.

items.q: Two heterozygotes are crossed and 500 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be homozygous dominant.
items.s: One quarter of the progeny are pure for the dominant form; 500 / 4 = 125.

items.q: A sample of 153 diploid individuals is taken from a population. State the number of copies of an autosomal gene present in the sample.
items.s: Every diploid individual carries two copies; 2 x 153 = 306.

items.q: Two parents heterozygous at both of two independently assorting loci are crossed and 896 offspring are obtained. Give the number expected to show both dominant characters.
items.s: The double dominant class fills nine parts of sixteen; 9 x 896 / 16 = 504.

items.q: In a cross between two double heterozygotes, 2992 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to show the dominant character of the first locus with the hidden character of the second.
items.s: That class fills three parts of sixteen; 3 x 2992 / 16 = 561.

items.q: A cross between two individuals heterozygous at both of two loci gives 1712 offspring. Give the number expected to show both hidden characters.
items.s: The double hidden class fills one part of sixteen; 1712 / 16 = 107.

items.q: A test cross yields 88 recombinant offspring out of 200 examined. State the distance between the two loci in map units, to two decimal places.
items.s: The separation in map units is the percentage of recombinants; 100 x 88 / 200 = 44.

items.q: Two loci lie 10 map units apart and 1200 offspring are produced by a test cross. Give the number of recombinant offspring expected.
items.s: The recombining fraction is 10 per cent of the progeny; 10 x 1200 / 100 = 120.

items.q: Aa is crossed with Aa and 472 offspring are counted. Give the number expected to be heterozygous.
items.s: Half the progeny of two heterozygotes carry two different forms; 472 / 2 = 236.

items.q: One form of a gene is not completely dominant over the other, so three classes appear in the ratio one to two to one. Of 576 offspring, give the number in the middle class.
items.s: The middle class fills two parts of four; 2 x 576 / 4 = 288.

the observable character that an organism actually shows

the random distribution of members of different gene pairs among reproductive cells so that one pair does not influence another
a reproductive cell that carries a single set of structures bearing the genes
the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme

a change that arises without any outside agent being applied

a trait expressed in only one of the two sexes although the genes for it lie in both
the condensed inactive copy of an X structure seen in the cells of a female
the passing of a character from a father to his daughters and then to his grandsons
items.s: criss cross inheritance: the passing of a character from a father to his daughters and then to his grandsons. The other options describe sex limited character, hemizygous, Barr body.

items.q: repulsion phase may be defined as
o: the arrangement in which a dominant form and a hidden form lie on the same member of a pair
the reduction in the chance of a second exchange close to a first one
a line drawing in which the order of genes and the distances between them are shown
the arrangement in which the two dominant forms lie on the same member of a pair
items.s: repulsion phase: the arrangement in which a dominant form and a hidden form lie on the same member of a pair. The other options describe genetic map, interference, coupling phase.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains aneuploidy.
o: the condition of having more than two complete sets of structures bearing the genes in a cell
a change in a body cell, which is not passed to the offspring
the condition of having one such structure too many or too few in a cell
a change of one base pair in the sequence of a gene
items.s: aneuploidy: the condition of having one such structure too many or too few in a cell. The other options describe polyploidy, point mutation, somatic mutation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a structure carrying genes that plays no part in deciding the sex of an organism”
o: autosome
criss cross inheritance
heterogametic sex
sex chromosome
items.s: autosome is a structure carrying genes that plays no part in deciding the sex of an organism.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the grouping of bases into triplets that fixes how a message is interpreted”
o: reading frame
translation
codon
intron
items.s: reading frame is the grouping of bases into triplets that fixes how a message is interpreted.

items.q: homozygous may be defined as
o: the form of a gene whose effect is hidden whenever a different form is present
carrying two identical forms of a gene at the same place on the two partner structures
the observable character that an organism actually shows
a pair of matings in which the characters contributed by the two parents are interchanged
items.s: homozygous: carrying two identical forms of a gene at the same place on the two partner structures. The other options describe recessive allele, phenotype, reciprocal cross.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains parental generation.
o: the random distribution of members of different gene pairs among reproductive cells so that one pair does not influence another
the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme
a mating of an offspring with one of its own parents
a reproductive cell that carries a single set of structures bearing the genes
items.s: parental generation: the two stocks chosen at the start of a crossing programme. The other options describe back cross, independent assortment, gamete.

items.q: “the situation in which both forms of a gene are fully expressed in the same individual” is the definition of
o: penetrance
codominance
incomplete dominance
modifying gene
items.s: codominance is the situation in which both forms of a gene are fully expressed in the same individual.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the existence of more than two forms of the same gene in a population”
o: incomplete dominance
multiple alleles
codominance
expressivity
items.s: multiple alleles is the existence of more than two forms of the same gene in a population.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains chromatid.
o: the constricted region where the two threads of a duplicated structure are joined
the count of structures in a reproductive cell, one from each pair
one of the two identical threads formed when a structure duplicates before division
the pairing of corresponding structures along their length before any exchange takes place
items.s: chromatid: one of the two identical threads formed when a structure duplicates before division. The other options describe haploid number, synapsis, centromere.
